value.value: Long-Term Effects of a Sectoral Advancement Strategy: Costs, Benefits, and Impacts from the WorkAdvance Demonstration
MDRC’s 2020 long-term randomized evaluation and benefit-cost analysis of four WorkAdvance sector-training providers.
https://www.mdrc.org/work/publications/long-term-effects-sectoral-advancement-strategy
WorkAdvance sectoral career-advancement model
A five-component sector-training model: screening, career readiness, occupational training, placement, and postemployment advancement support.
https://www.mdrc.org/work/publications/long-term-effects-sectoral-advancement-strategy
WorkAdvance randomly assigned 2,564 adults across four provider sites.
The 2011–2013 evaluation assigned 1,293 people to WorkAdvance and 1,271 to control services. Site-specific analysis is primary; pooled results can mask provider variation.
Executive Summary, pp. ES-2–ES-3.
WorkAdvance pooled 2018 earnings effect: +$2,716.
Across all four sites, 2018 earnings were $26,419 for WorkAdvance and $23,703 for control participants. This pooled effect is not a provider-specific result.
Table ES.3; Executive Summary p. ES-6.
USD difference in total 2018 earnings, WorkAdvance minus control; National Directory of New Hires data.
WorkAdvance pooled 2018 $30,000-or-more earnings effect: +6.4 percentage points.
In the pooled sample, 40.0% of WorkAdvance and 33.7% of control participants earned at least $30,000 in 2018. The threshold is report-specific and the pooled result masks provider variation.
Table ES.3; Executive Summary p. ES-6.
Percentage-point difference in earning $30,000 or more in 2018, WorkAdvance minus control.
